easy.def: A picture.
examples: The image is clear.
I saw an image.
The image shows a bird.

more.def: A picture or likeness of something.
examples: The image on the screen was clear.
The telescope took an image of the moon.
She saw her image in the mirror.

easy.def: A picture in your mind.
examples: I have an image of home.
The image stayed in my mind.
She had an image of the beach.

more.def: A picture of something that you form in your mind.
examples: I have an image of my house in my mind.
The image of the sunset stayed with her.
He tried to form an image of the new city.

easy.def: Words that make pictures in your mind.
examples: The poem has lovely imagery.
I like the imagery in that story.
The imagery made me see the sea.

more.def: Descriptive language or pictures that help the reader see, hear or feel what is being described.
examples: The poet used imagery of golden leaves to describe autumn.
Her story is full of imagery about the quiet forest.
Strong imagery in a book helps readers picture the scene.

easy.def: Possible to think of.
examples: Every color imaginable was there.
It was the best day imaginable.
They had every toy imaginable.

more.def: Able to be thought of or pictured in your mind.
examples: The store sold every color imaginable.
It was the happiest day imaginable.
They tried every game imaginable at the party.

easy.def: Not real, only in your mind.
examples: She has an imaginary friend.
A dragon is imaginary.
The monster is imaginary.

more.def: Made up in the mind and not real.
examples: My little brother has an imaginary friend named Max.
The dragon in the story is an imaginary creature.
She drew an imaginary map of a make-believe island.

easy.def: The part of your mind that makes pictures of things that are not real.
examples: She has a good imagination.
Use your imagination.
His imagination is wild.

more.def: The ability to picture new things or ideas in your mind.
examples: She has a great imagination and loves to invent stories.
Use your imagination to draw a new animal.
His imagination turned the box into a spaceship.

easy.def: Good at thinking up new ideas.
examples: She is an imaginative girl.
His story is imaginative.
An imaginative child made a fort.

more.def: Good at thinking up new and creative ideas.
examples: The imaginative girl turned a box into a spaceship.
His imaginative story had talking trees.
An imaginative artist painted a purple sky.

easy.def: To make a picture in your mind.
examples: Imagine you can fly like a bird!
I imagine I am a pirate.
Can you imagine a pink elephant?

more.def: To form a picture or idea in your mind of something that is not in front of you.
examples: Try to imagine what our town looked like one hundred years ago.
Imagine how cold it must be at the North Pole.
I cannot imagine life without music.

easy.def: Making pictures of things inside the body or far away.
examples: The doctor used imaging.
Imaging shows a bone.
Space imaging shows planets.

more.def: The process of making pictures of things, such as with a scan or telescope.
examples: Doctors use imaging to see inside the body.
Space imaging gave us clear photos of Jupiter.
Scientists use imaging to make maps of the ocean floor.

easy.def: When things are not equal.
examples: There is an imbalance on the scale.
The seesaw has an imbalance.
An imbalance made the table wobble.

more.def: A lack of balance, or a difference in amount between two things.
examples: An imbalance in weight made the boat tip.
There was an imbalance in the number of boys and girls.
The scale showed an imbalance between the two sides.

easy.def: To copy what someone does or says.
examples: My parrot likes to imitate me.
I imitate my sister.
Can you imitate a cat?

more.def: To copy the way a person, animal or thing looks, sounds or acts.
examples: Parrots can imitate the sounds of human voices.
The comedian could imitate the way each teacher talked.
Young birds learn to sing by listening and then imitating their parents.

easy.def: A copy of something.
examples: The toy is an imitation.
This is an imitation of a real gem.
She did an imitation of a cat.

more.def: A copy of something, or the act of copying how someone acts or sounds.
examples: The toy is an imitation of a real car.
This necklace is an imitation of a real gem.
She did a funny imitation of a cat.

easy.def: Perfectly clean.
examples: The room is immaculate.
An immaculate kitchen.
Her shirt is immaculate.

more.def: Perfectly clean and neat.
examples: The kitchen was immaculate after we cleaned.
He wore an immaculate white shirt.
Her room is always immaculate.

easy.def: Not grown up yet in mind or body.
examples: The baby bird is immature.
It was immature to yell.
The immature plant is small.

more.def: Not fully grown, or acting younger than you really are.
examples: The immature bird cannot fly yet.
It was immature to yell at her friend.
The immature plant is only a few inches tall.

easy.def: Happening right now.
examples: I need an immediate answer.
Help is immediate.
The immediate need is water.

more.def: Happening at once, without any delay.
examples: The teacher asked for an immediate answer.
The fire alarm needs an immediate response.
The immediate need was food and water.

easy.def: Very close or next.
examples: The immediate family is here.
The immediate area is clear.
The immediate neighbors are nice.

more.def: Closest in space or in relationship.
examples: The whole immediate family came to the party.
There are no shops in the immediate area.
The immediate neighbors helped with the move.

easy.def: Right now; with no waiting.
examples: Come immediately.
She answered immediately.
He left immediately.

more.def: At once; with no delay.
examples: Come here immediately.
The firefighters arrived immediately.
She answered the phone immediately.

easy.def: Very big.
examples: The whale is immense.
The immense tree fell.
An immense cave.

more.def: Extremely large.
examples: The blue whale is an immense animal.
An immense tree stood in the park.
The cave was immense and dark.

easy.def: To put something fully into water.
examples: Immerse the cloth in water.
She immersed her feet in the pool.
He immersed the cup.

more.def: To put something completely under a liquid, or to be deeply involved in something.
examples: Immerse the eggs in boiling water.
She immersed herself in a good book.
He immersed his hands in the warm soapy water.

easy.def: A person who moves to live in a new country.
examples: My neighbor is an immigrant.
The immigrant came by ship.
Many immigrants live in our town.

more.def: A person who comes to live in a country that is not the one where they were born.
examples: My grandmother was an immigrant who came to America by ship when she was ten.
Many immigrants bring new foods, music and customs to their new home.
The immigrant family opened a small bakery on our street.

easy.def: Never dying.
examples: The gods were immortal.
An immortal hero.
Nothing is immortal.

more.def: Living forever and never dying.
examples: The gods in the story were immortal.
The hero's fame seemed immortal.
No person is immortal.

easy.def: A strong hit.
examples: The impact broke the glass.
The ball hit with great impact.
The crash had a loud impact.

more.def: The force of one thing hitting another, or a strong effect.
examples: The impact of the ball broke the window.
The helmet protects your head from impact.
The new rule had a big impact on the school.

easy.def: Not wanting to wait.
examples: His impatience showed.
She tapped her foot in impatience.
Impatience made him rush.

more.def: A feeling of being unable to wait or put up with delay.
examples: His impatience grew as the bus kept being late.
His impatience showed as he kept checking the clock.
The long line tested everyone's impatience.

easy.def: Not wanting to wait.
examples: The child was impatient.
I am impatient for my turn.
He grew impatient.

more.def: Not willing to wait, or easily annoyed when you have to wait.
examples: The child was impatient and tapped his foot.
I am impatient to open my gift.
She grew impatient waiting in the long line.

easy.def: Not perfect.
examples: The cup is imperfect.
I saw an imperfect circle.
My drawing is imperfect.

more.def: Having a fault or mistake, and not perfect.
examples: The cup has a crack, so it is imperfect.
I drew an imperfect circle, but it was fine.
No one is perfect; we are all imperfect.

easy.def: A small fault.
examples: There is an imperfection.
The vase has an imperfection.
I found an imperfection.

more.def: A small fault or flaw that makes something not perfect.
examples: There was a tiny imperfection in the glass.
The vase had an imperfection that made it special.
I found an imperfection in my drawing.

easy.def: Not friendly or personal.
examples: The letter was impersonal.
An impersonal note.
The big room felt impersonal.

more.def: Not showing personal feeling or friendliness.
examples: The letter was cold and impersonal.
The big office felt impersonal.
An impersonal machine answered the phone.

easy.def: To act or sound like someone else.
examples: He can impersonate a duck.
She impersonated her teacher.
I impersonate a cat.

more.def: To act or talk like another person or animal, often to be funny or to trick people.
examples: My brother can impersonate a duck so well that the dog looked for it.
She impersonated our teacher, and the class laughed.
The actor impersonated a famous singer.

easy.def: Copying how someone talks and acts.
examples: He did an impersonation.
The impersonation was funny.
She did a bird impersonation.

more.def: The act of copying the voice and actions of another person or animal.
examples: He did a funny impersonation of the teacher.
Her bird impersonation fooled the dog.
The class loved his impersonation of a monkey.

easy.def: A person who copies how someone talks and acts.
examples: The impersonator was funny.
An impersonator did a show.
She is an impersonator.

more.def: A performer who copies the voice and actions of another person to be funny.
examples: The impersonator did a funny show copying a singer.
She is a good impersonator of animal sounds.
An impersonator made the crowd laugh.

easy.def: To say something without saying it directly.
examples: Her smile implies she is happy.
The dark clouds imply rain.
His look implied he was upset.

more.def: To suggest something without saying it directly.
examples: Dark clouds imply that rain is on the way.
His silence implied that he was angry.
The sign implies that the road is closed.

easy.def: Not polite.
examples: It is impolite to shout.
The impolite boy pushed.
That was an impolite thing to say.

more.def: Not showing good manners or respect for others.
examples: It is impolite to talk with your mouth full.
The impolite visitor did not say thank you.
She felt it was impolite to interrupt.

easy.def: To bring goods into a country from another place.
examples: We import fruit.
They imported tea.
The store imports toys.

more.def: To bring in goods from another country to sell or use.
examples: We import bananas from far away.
The store imports tea from India.
The country imports cars from other places.

easy.def: A product that is brought from another country.
examples: The coffee is an import.
Imports come on ships.
The toy is an import.

more.def: A product that is brought into a country from another country.
examples: The coffee is an import from South America.
Imports often come on big ships.
The shop sells imports from many lands.

easy.def: How much something matters.
examples: The importance of sleep is clear.
He knows the importance of water.
The importance is great.

more.def: The quality of being very useful, valuable or needed.
examples: The teacher explained the importance of sleep.
He understands the importance of water.
The importance of the job was clear.

easy.def: Something that matters a lot.
examples: It is important to wash your hands.
It is important to be kind.
Sleep is important for kids.

more.def: Having great value or meaning; mattering a lot.
examples: Getting enough sleep is important for staying healthy.
The mayor has an important job in our town.
It is important to look both ways before you cross.

easy.def: In a way that matters a lot.
examples: Importantly, we are safe.
More importantly, we won.
Importantly, wear a helmet.

more.def: In a way that shows something is of great importance.
examples: Importantly, everyone is safe.
More importantly, he said sorry.
Most importantly, wear a helmet.

easy.def: Something that cannot happen.
examples: It is an impossibility.
Flying alone is an impossibility.
The task was an impossibility.

more.def: Something that cannot be done or cannot happen.
examples: Counting every grain of sand is an impossibility.
It was an impossibility to finish by noon.
The impossibility of the plan was clear.

easy.def: Not able to happen or be done.
examples: It is impossible to touch the moon.
It is impossible to count all the stars.
The knot was impossible to undo.

more.def: Not able to be done or to happen.
examples: It seemed impossible to finish the puzzle, but we did it.
The heavy snow made it impossible to drive.
Nothing is impossible if you keep trying, said the coach.

easy.def: A person who pretends to be someone else.
examples: The impostor wore a mask.
Who is the impostor?
The impostor fooled us.

more.def: A person who pretends to be someone else in order to trick others.
examples: In the mystery game, one player is secretly an impostor.
The prince was really an impostor who had borrowed the royal robe.
The impostor was found out when he could not remember the answer.

easy.def: To make someone think well of you.
examples: The trick impressed us.
She impressed the teacher.
His jump impressed everyone.

more.def: To make someone feel respect or admiration.
examples: The magic trick impressed the whole class.
She impressed the teacher with her story.
His high jump impressed the crowd.

easy.def: The feeling you get about something when you first meet it.
examples: She made a good impression.
My first impression was good.
I got a good impression of the school.

more.def: An idea or feeling about someone or something that you form when you first meet or see them.
examples: He made a good impression on his new teacher.
My first impression of the house was that it was cozy.
I had the impression that the test was easy.

easy.def: Easily influenced by others.
examples: Young children are impressionable.
An impressionable child copies.
Be careful with impressionable kids.

more.def: Easy to influence, especially because of being young.
examples: Young children are impressionable and copy what they see.
The impressionable boy copied his big brother.
Teachers know that impressionable students watch them.

easy.def: So good that people admire it.
examples: The tall tower is impressive.
Her jump was impressive.
The show was impressive.

more.def: Making people admire it because it is great or very large.
examples: The tall tower was impressive.
Her high jump was impressive.
The magician's tricks were impressive.

easy.def: A mark made by pressing on something.
examples: I left an imprint in the sand.
An imprint of a hand.
The foot made an imprint.

more.def: A mark or a picture that is made by pressing something into a soft surface.
examples: My foot left an imprint in the wet sand.
The coin left an imprint in the clay.
She pressed her hand into the cement to leave an imprint.

easy.def: To press a mark into something.
examples: I imprinted my hand.
The stamp imprinted the paper.
Imprint the design.

more.def: To press or stamp a mark into something.
examples: She imprinted her hand in the wet clay.
The stamp imprinted a star on each page.
The seal imprinted the shape of an eagle in the wax.

easy.def: To keep someone locked up.
examples: The king imprisoned the thief.
The giant imprisoned the elf.
They imprisoned the bird.

more.def: To put someone in a prison or keep them locked up so that they cannot leave.
examples: In the fairy tale, the wicked king imprisoned the princess in a tall tower.
The judge ordered that the thief be imprisoned.
The cage imprisoned the bird until we set it free.

easy.def: Not right or not suitable.
examples: That is improper.
Using the wrong tool is improper.
It was improper to shout.

more.def: Not correct or not suitable for the time or place.
examples: It is improper to talk during the show.
He used the improper tool, so the screw bent.
An improper answer was written on the test.

easy.def: To get better.
examples: I practice to improve my drawing.
My reading improves each week.
We can improve the fort with a roof.

more.def: To make something better or to become better.
examples: Her reading improved after she practiced every night.
The weather improved in the afternoon.
He added salt to improve the taste of the soup.

easy.def: Getting better.
examples: I see improvement.
There was an improvement in my reading.
The improvement is big.

more.def: A change that makes something better.
examples: I see a big improvement in your writing.
The new road is an improvement.
Her reading showed steady improvement.

easy.def: To make something up as you go, without planning.
examples: The actors improvise.
I improvised a song.
She improvised a tent from a blanket.

more.def: To make or do something on the spot, using what you have, without planning.
examples: The actors improvised the scene and made up words as they went.
We improvised a tent from blankets and chairs.
She improvised a song about her cat.

easy.def: A sudden urge to do something.
examples: I had an impulse to laugh.
She bought it on impulse.
He followed his impulse.

more.def: A sudden wish to do something without thinking about it first.
examples: I had an impulse to jump in the puddle.
She bought the toy on impulse.
He fought the impulse to shout.

easy.def: Doing things fast without thinking first.
examples: He is an impulsive child.
It was an impulsive choice.
Her impulsive jump.

more.def: Acting quickly because of a sudden feeling, without stopping to think first.
examples: She was impulsive and jumped in the pool without testing the water.
It was an impulsive choice to buy the bright red hat.
An impulsive child might grab a toy without asking.
